label: Define local records
artifact: Three training assets + one bounded record schema
title: Start with the record that must survive a reload.
detail: A fictional equipment inspection captures an asset, its condition, three checks and optional notes. Drafts can be incomplete; submitted records must satisfy the full schema.

label: Protect the record lifecycle
artifact: Explicit draft saves + read-only submitted records
title: Make each saved change deliberate.
detail: Save draft preserves unfinished work. Submission requires an asset, condition and all three checks. Pending writes lock the editor; timestamp checks reject stale saves from another tab.

label: Prepare offline availability
artifact: A scoped shell cache alongside IndexedDB records
title: Keep the notebook available when the connection drops.
detail: A successful online visit prepares the application shell. After the service worker takes control, that shell can reload offline while inspection records remain in separate browser storage.

label: Restore backups atomically
artifact: Validated JSON + an all-or-nothing add transaction
title: Restore the whole batch, or leave every record unchanged.
detail: Validate the backup before opening a write transaction. Enforce the 1,000-record limit and add each ID without overwriting. An existing ID aborts the entire import, including queued new records.

label: Challenge failure boundaries
artifact: 35 domain tests + 20 browser checks, recorded 13 Oct 2026
title: Test the interruptions as well as the happy path.
detail: The development record covers pending-write locks, stale tabs, duplicate rollback, backup limits and offline reload. Observed failures led to monotonic edit timestamps and a larger UTF-8 backup bound.

label: Package and reproduce
artifact: Standalone demo, source, architecture and dated evidence
title: Leave a small notebook that can be inspected end to end.
detail: Keep the browser demo, source archive and development evidence together. The implementation has no external runtime dependencies, server or multi-user sync; records belong to the current browser origin.
